practice_tasks.task_intent: Produce sophisticated motion graphics on the computer, relying on one's own creative judgment.
practice_tasks.task_intent_note: DreamCo paraphrase of the cited O*NET task's purpose, in original wording; not O*NET text.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. A city transit agency wants a 20-second silent animated explainer, for station screens, showing how to tap a contactless card or phone to pay. Write the production plan and creative rationale: a short storyboard (six to eight frames with timing), the visual style and color palette tied to the agency's brand and accessibility, how motion guides attention without text, the software and file formats you will use, and how you will test that riders understand it without sound.

rubric.description: Storyboard communicates the steps in sequence with timing that fits 20 seconds.
Style, contrast and motion choices support comprehension, including for viewers with low vision or limited English.
Names tools and output specs and includes a comprehension test with riders.

reference_answer_outline: Frames: approach gate, hold card near reader, light or check mark feedback, gate opens, phone variant.
Brand palette with high contrast; large icons; no essential text.
Motion: highlight reader with gentle pulse; ease-in timing; loop cleanly.
Tools: vector design and motion graphics software; export at screen resolution and frame rate.
Test with ten riders: can they describe the steps after one viewing?

practice_tasks.task_intent: Decide how big images and text should be, how they are arranged on the page, and which typefaces and sizes to use.
practice_tasks.task_intent_note: DreamCo paraphrase of the cited O*NET task's purpose, in original wording; not O*NET text.
practice_tasks.label: DreamCo-original practice prompt
practice_tasks.authorship: DreamCo-original, authored by Grok-Edu-Career-Pathways (AI), not human-reviewed
practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. Design a poster (24 by 36 inches) for a free community jazz festival with a headline, date and location, five performer names, a sponsor logo strip and a QR code. Write the layout and typography specification: grid and margins, the visual hierarchy (what is read first, second, third), typeface choices and sizes in points with reasons, image placement and scale, color and contrast, and how the design adapts to a 1080 by 1920 pixel social media version.

rubric.description: Arrangement makes the most important information readable first from a distance.
Typefaces, sizes and spacing are specified and justified for legibility and mood.
Explains how the layout adapts to a vertical digital format without losing hierarchy.

reference_answer_outline: Grid: 12 columns, margins about 1 inch, generous whitespace.
Hierarchy: festival name, then date and place, then performers, then sponsors and QR code.
Type: display face for the headline at large size; clean sans serif for details; at most two families.
Image: full-bleed illustration with text on a calm area; contrast checked.
Social version: stacked layout, larger date, QR code replaced by link.

practice_tasks.task_intent: Work with front-end and back-end developers so a website project is delivered completely.
practice_tasks.task_intent_note: DreamCo paraphrase of the cited O*NET task's purpose, in original wording; not O*NET text.
practice_tasks.label: DreamCo-original practice prompt
practice_tasks.authorship: DreamCo-original, authored by Grok-Edu-Career-Pathways (AI), not human-reviewed
practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. You designed an online exhibit for a local history museum with scroll-triggered animations, an interactive timeline and an image zoom viewer, to be built by one front-end and one back-end developer. Write the collaboration plan: how you specify animations (timing, easing, reduced-motion alternatives), the content model the back end must support (timeline entries, image sets, captions, credits), performance budgets for images and scripts, how you pair with developers during build, and acceptance testing.

rubric.description: Animation and interaction specs are concrete enough to build and include accessibility alternatives.
Defines a content model and performance budgets that developers can implement.
Describes pairing, feedback loops and acceptance tests.

reference_answer_outline: Motion specs with durations and easing; prefers-reduced-motion fallback.
Content model fields: date, title, text, images, alt text, credits.
Budgets: page weight limit, responsive images, lazy loading.
Weekly pairing sessions and a shared issues board.
Acceptance: device matrix, keyboard navigation, screen reader check, performance score.

practice_tasks.task_intent: Make digital objects and characters look believable through careful handling of lighting, surface color and texture, shadows and see-through materials, or by bringing still images to life.
practice_tasks.task_intent_note: DreamCo paraphrase of the cited O*NET task's purpose, in original wording; not O*NET text.
practice_tasks.label: DreamCo-original practice prompt
practice_tasks.authorship: DreamCo-original, authored by Grok-Edu-Career-Pathways (AI), not human-reviewed
practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. A kitchenware company needs a photorealistic 3D render of a glass-and-steel kettle for its website, matching studio product photography. Write the lighting, materials and rendering plan: the light setup (key, fill, rim, environment map), physically based material settings for brushed steel, clear glass with water inside and a rubber handle, how you handle reflections, caustics and shadows, the render settings, and how you compare the result with reference photos.

rubric.description: Light setup is purposeful and mimics studio product photography.
Material parameters (roughness, index of refraction, anisotropy) are appropriate for each material.
Describes how renders are evaluated against real photos and adjusted.

reference_answer_outline: Large soft key, fill card, rim light for edges, neutral HDRI for reflections.
Steel: metallic with anisotropic roughness; glass: refractive index around 1.5; water slightly higher.
Shadows: soft contact shadow; caustics enabled or faked for speed.
Render samples and denoising settings; output color space.
Side-by-side with reference shots; adjust highlights and reflections.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. A neighborhood bakery wants a new logo and storefront sign. Describe your concept phase: how you gather the brief (values, audience, competitors), six thumbnail directions in words, how you narrow to three rough sketches, how you present them to the owners and capture feedback, and how you revise without losing the concept. Include the questions you ask when feedback is vague (such as 'make it pop').

rubric.description: Concepts clearly connect to the brief and are distinct.
Presentation explains rationale and gathers specific, usable feedback.
Revisions respond to feedback while protecting legibility and concept, with documented approvals.

reference_answer_outline: Brief questionnaire and a mood board.
Thumbnails: hand-lettered script, wheat icon, vintage badge, minimalist wordmark, illustrative storefront, geometric bread shape.
Three roughs shown on a mockup sign at real scale.
Clarifying questions: which part should stand out, what feeling is missing, show an example you like.
Revision round with change log and owner sign-off.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. A food-rescue nonprofit hires you to redesign its website to recruit volunteers and donors. Write the pre-production plan: discovery activities, two mood boards described in words with the reasoning behind each, a storyboard of the volunteer sign-up journey from home page to confirmation, content and asset inventory, roles and approvals, and a six-week timeline with milestones and review points.

rubric.description: Discovery identifies users, goals and constraints before visual work.
Mood boards and storyboard are specific and tied to goals.
Timeline has milestones, review points and dependencies on client content.

reference_answer_outline: Discovery: stakeholder interview, analytics review, three volunteer interviews.
Mood board A: warm, community photography; B: bold, data-driven impact graphics.
Storyboard: home, volunteer page, choose shift, form, confirmation email.
Inventory: photos, impact numbers, copy, logos.
Weeks 1 to 6 with approvals after mood boards and wireframes.
